cards.title: The Protégé Problem
cards.instruction: Treat another player as someone you trained. Offer corrections, backhanded praise, and reminders of your influence.

cards.title: Credit for the Impossible
cards.instruction: Make someone acknowledge that you understood, predicted, or accepted the impossible truth before anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's use what I taught you. I drew that floating staircase last week. Mention the date.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can all see it now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're nearly doing it my way. I drew the handrail while you called it nonsense.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Loud enough for the people using my prediction to get upstairs.

mechanism: A uses its pupil sketching and projection lessons to demand public credit for predicting a physically impossible staircase.
confusable: Not mere ownership of artwork: A requires acknowledgment that its drawing preceded the now-visible impossible structure.
comparison: Dated visual prediction versus belief before a cupboard spoke.
